title: Product-space inner product
statement: For a finite set $\Omega$, a probability mass function $\pi$ on $\Omega$, a natural number $n$, and real-valued functions $f,g$ on $\Omega^n$, define their product-space inner product as their probability-weighted inner product under the independent product distribution with marginal $\pi$ at each coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
